notes: Explore idea: sudoers-check, a static checker for sudoers policy (browser + zero-dependency Node CLI). It reports rules that grant root without looking like it (editors/pagers/interactive clients, shells/interpreters/exec-capable tools with open args, file writers and account tools, ALL minus a command, writable paths, directory or glob commands, SETENV, env_keep LD_PRELOAD, !env_reset, !authenticate) and rules that never take effect (a NOPASSWD rule a later %sudo rule overrides; sudoers.d files with a dot in the name), plus a list of who can become root. Verification: the parser was compared with sudo's own cvtsudoers -e -f json (sudo 1.9.15p5, installed in the container). It matches on 41 grammar cases (1 skipped: cvtsudoers emits invalid JSON for CWD=) and on all 49 rule entries of the sudoers(5) EXAMPLES section (fixture, ISC notice kept). The comparison found two real bugs, fixed before merge: LOG_INPUT/MAIL tag opposites, and a sha224 digest inside a Cmnd_Alias. visudo -c accepts every fixture. The stock Ubuntu 24.04 sudoers produces 0 findings. A cp -t wildcard escape was confirmed in a scratch dir. 91 node tests pass. Local workflow sweep: first sweep found the inherited-keys failure (fixed); re-run results in the PR. Human-hours estimate: a security engineer, about 16 h.
